classifiedFindings.label: L-21

classification.assetImpact: Protocol-own revenue accounting: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.mintDebt (ratio% of dispatched USDS, realised by pull() as phUSD minted to the protocol's own recipient) silently stays 0 for every index-4 mint while the DefaultDispatchHook is wired. No user funds move; no third party gains; USDS still flows into POL. The shortfall is reconstructible from Dispatched/mint events and can be made good by an owner mint. Secondary facet: separate-tx setDispatcher/replaceDispatcher ordering opens a fail-LOUD index-4 mint outage window (OnlyDispatcher revert), no loss.
attackPath: 1. Owner deploys UniPoolerV2 (ctor wires no-op DefaultDispatchHook)
2. Cutover replaceDispatcher(4) executes before / without setHook(BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook)
3. Every index-4 mint succeeds; _dispatch has no non-default-hook guard; onDispatch is a no-op
4. mintDebt never accrues; no revert, no event signalling the omission
classification.likelihood: low-medium - requires an owner sequencing omission in a multi-step, multi-contract cutover; non-obvious because NudgeRatchet (M-04 fix) fails closed in the identical situation
classification.assumptions: Non-malicious owner; setHook skipped or reordered in the story-048 cutover

classifiedFindings.justification: Non-obvious Law-3 footgun, so in scope, but impact is a recoverable, attacker-less under-accrual of the protocol's own mint-debt (no theft, no user loss, no availability loss). Severity follows the closest sibling L-09 (Uniboost, same base-class fail-open, open Low) rather than M-04: M-04's Medium predates the established sibling precedent and the M-04 fix is per-concrete. Q-08's wont-fix rationale (live, no retrofit) does not transfer to undeployed UniPoolerV2 - a pre-deploy guard is cheap.
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Medium is arguable on the M-04 precedent (same class filed Medium). Kept Low because the debt is protocol-own revenue, recoverable by an owner mint, and no party profits. If the owner considers mintDebt load-bearing for phUSD backing/emission accounting, re-weigh to Medium.
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Add a concrete-only guard (stored defaultHook compared in _dispatch, or hookTypeId() on the pooler hook) pre-deploy, with a story-048 verbatim-clause waiver; otherwise setHook before or atomically with replaceDispatcher(4), and verify a DebtAccrued on the first index-4 mint.

classifiedFindings.label: L-22

classification.assetImpact: Protocol-owned liquidity only: per-zap extraction ~0.44*t*Delta (ECON-001: $1,000 zap -> $2.21/$4.43/$8.87/$13.34 at t = 0.5/1/2/3%). Protocol owns ~100% of LP post-cutover, so searcher profit == protocol loss. No user funds.
attackPath: 1. Searcher observes public keeper pool(sUSDSIn, minPhusdOut, minLP)
2. Front-runs with sUSDS->phUSD buy, moving price up to the keeper tolerance
3. Keeper swap+addLiquidity executes at worse price; floors pass
4. Searcher back-runs, capturing ~0.44*t*Delta
classification.likelihood: medium - every public keeper call is sandwichable, but extraction is capped by keeper-chosen tolerance
classification.assumptions: Keeper submits publicly with tolerance t; addLiquidity mins are 0/0 by design

classifiedFindings.justification: Bounded, keeper-controlled MEV on POL; successor instance of open Low L-06 on the same pattern. Not Medium: loss per event is capped by an operator parameter and eliminated by private submission.

classifiedFindings.label: L-23

classification.assetImpact: POL only. Same-block batching of UniPoolerV2.pool and PromotionUniV2_Eth Leg A on the shared phUSD/sUSDS pair either self-reverts (1k zap moves Leg A out 2.83%, Leg A moves zap 3.26%) or forces tolerances >= ~3.5% that a single front-run harvests across both calls.
attackPath: 1. Keeper quotes both calls against the same pre-state and submits in one block
2. Either the second call reverts on its floor (self-DoS), or keeper widens tolerance
3. With widened tolerance a searcher front-runs once and extracts against both calls
classification.likelihood: low-medium - requires keeper batching on stale quotes
classification.assumptions: Keeper batches both calls; public submission

classifiedFindings.justification: New cross-contract coupling created by a4d80f4's venue change; extraction remains tolerance-bounded and POL-only, so same severity tier as L-15/L-06. Non-obvious operational coupling (keeper footgun).
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Not a severity borderline - a DUPLICATE borderline: owner may rule that wont-fix L-15 e64f73d629 already covers it. Disclose L-15's verbatim triageReason in the submission; note its 'all 5 floors present' premise is only parametric (4 accept 0).

classifiedFindings.label: Q-19
classifiedFindings.fingerprintNote: Facet A keeps the consolidated fingerprint (its root cause IS pair-not-bound-to-router-factory).

classification.assetImpact: If deployed with a token-matching pair from a different factory, pool()/quotePool size from _pair while the router executes on the factory pair: mis-sized zaps bounded by floors; LP lands as a different token (rescuable).
attackPath: Owner-supplied constructor argument only; no third-party path
classification.assumptions: Deploy script passes a non-canonical pair

classifiedFindings.justification: Missing deploy-time validation (require(factory.getPair(sUSDS, phUSD) == pair_)). Supplying the wrong pair address is an obvious-consequence misconfiguration (story-faithfulness already suppressed it under Law 3), floors bound any loss, and LP is rescuable. QA hardening.

classifiedFindings.label: L-24
classifiedFindings.fingerprintNote: PROPOSED new fingerprint for the split; finding-manager to mint. If the owner prefers the consolidated entry, fold back under 0983961...

classification.assetImpact: Cutover availability: a third party createPair()s and mints dust at a skewed ratio before the protocol seed, so the cutover's reserves==(0,0) precondition fails. No fund loss in-repo: the fail-loud precondition halts the script. Loss arises only if the operator takes the unsafe workaround (router addLiquidity with zero mins into the skewed pair), letting arbitrage take value from the ~100%-protocol LP.
attackPath: 1. Before cutover, griefer calls factory.createPair(sUSDS, phUSD) (if absent) and mints dust at an arbitrary ratio
2. Cutover precondition 0 (empty reserves) reverts
3. Safe recovery: pre-arbitrage the dust pair to target ratio (profitable against the griefer) then seed via transfer+mint with a reserve-ratio assertion
4. Unsafe recovery: relax precondition / router-add with zero mins -> protocol seeds at the griefer's price and is arbitraged
classification.likelihood: low - griefer gains nothing and loses the skew to arbitrage; harm requires a further operator mistake
classification.assumptions: Pair is empty or absent at cutover time; operator chooses the recovery path

classifiedFindings.justification: Distinct actor (third party), vector and mitigation from facet A, hence split. Non-obvious (MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY permanence; 'permanently griefed' is overstated - the skew is cheaply and profitably corrected). Delay-only availability impact on a one-off cutover plus a documented-fallback footgun: Low, not Medium. Route to /audit-script on the cutover entry point.

classifiedFindings.label: L-25
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessNote: Falsifies story-048 / NatSpec claims that a front-run 'never [changes] the leftover' and that quotePool's expectedLP 'remains a valid floor' (true only for swap-style front-runs). story-048 is auto-complete. Filed under its security label L-25 at honest Low; spec-conformance report must cross-reference it (no separate F label, to avoid double-filing).
classifiedFindings.toolSeverityOverride: Failing invariants P1/P4/P8 (T3-R20-01, forge+medusa) carried a tool default of potential-high; overridden to Low on demonstrated impact.

classification.assetImpact: (a) Strand: 0.5% sUSDS donation -> 229.398 phUSD left on the pooler after a 100k zap (PoC). The phUSD is protocol-held, not lost; owner rescueERC20 recovers it. The attacker's donation (5,105.88 sUSDS, ~22x the stranded value) is absorbed into pair reserves owned ~100% by the pooler, so the protocol is net UP. (b) DoS: 2% donation -> pool() reverts UniPoolerV2__InsufficientLP(48746147894859096248178, 49179748976765704050059); attacker skim()s the donation back (gas-only, requires bundling or it is skimmed by any searcher). Dispatch/mint path unaffected (P9).
attackPath: 1. Attacker sees keeper pool(a, quote*0.99, quoteLP*0.99) in the public mempool
2. Bundles: transfer x sUSDS to pair (no sync) -> keeper tx -> pair.skim(attacker)
3. Keeper tx reverts InsufficientLP; attacker recovers x; repeat per keeper attempt
Alt: smaller x lets pool() succeed but strands phUSD (attacker forfeits x to LPs)
classification.likelihood: low - zero-profit griefing; requires bundling a public keeper tx; defeated by private submission or a keeper-side pair.sync()/skim() before pool()
classification.assumptions: Keeper submits publicly; pooler is ~100% LP post-cutover (strand case net-positive for protocol)
classification.externalRequirements: Attacker willing to pay gas per griefed call with no return

classifiedFindings.justification: No value leaves the protocol (strand is rescuable and paid for by the attacker at >= 22x; DoS is gas-only and permissionlessly neutralised by sync/skim). Availability impact is limited to delaying a keeper-only POL-compounding call; user mints are unaffected. C4 treats zero-profit, per-call griefing of a non-core keeper function with a trivial operational counter as Low, not Medium. The falsified spec claim is a real Law-2 defect, surfaced via faithfulness cross-reference.
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Medium would require sustained availability loss that matters: pool() delay does not affect users, funds, or the mint path, and keeper countermeasures (private RPC already recommended by L-22; sync() at top of pool()) are trivial. Re-weigh to Medium only if pool() latency becomes economically load-bearing (e.g., a time-sensitive peg defence relying on zaps).
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Call IUniswapV2Pair(pair).sync() (or skim to self) at the top of pool() before reading reserves; correct the NatSpec / story-048 claim.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-21

classification.assetImpact: Plan §5 sizes zaps against full Balancer depth (~33.8k/34.8k) but the V2 seed is the protocol's 62.9% (~19.1k sUSDS / 21.9k phUSD): phUSD crosses $1 at a ~$636 zap, not ~$1k, so the intended POL arb skim per zap is larger than the plan states.
attackPath: Keeper sizes zaps per plan -> overshoots $1 -> arbitrageurs skim the excess from POL (intended mechanism, mis-sized)
classification.likelihood: medium if plan numbers are used as-is

classifiedFindings.justification: Planning-document premise error affecting operator sizing of an intended (by-design) arb skim on POL; not a code defect and the skim itself is designed behaviour. Informational, carried in the QA bundle with sizing guidance (chunk pool() so post-zap spot <= $1).
